findings.reason: as written the crew case is unimplementable inside the node's fence, so §11 would either fail its own done-when or need `tests/test_spa_derived_flow.py` (and a fake-timer path) added to its write paths.
findings.text: §11's crew case ("a poll showing a changed run phase fetches `/_schedule` once ... after a minute fetches once ... the newly working run's bar then draws in flight") requires both a poll cadence and a render, and neither is reachable from §11's declared write paths: `tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py` runs `docs/ui/state-loader.js` under bare `node` with no React at all, and the only harness that renders `docs/ui/crew.jsx` is `tests/test_spa_derived_flow.py`, which is §10's write path and is not listed in §11 — and whose prelude stubs `useEffect`, `useState` and `setInterval` to no-ops, so it cannot drive a 3 s or 60 s cadence without being extended

findings.reason: a hard gate the mechanism cannot satisfy regardless of implementation needs its threshold restated (exclude the load request and count change events from the stream, or compare against windows+loads), otherwise the section is scored red on correct work.
findings.text: the coordinator clause "counts `/_index/power_convertor` requests in the served log over 30 minutes ... and the section holds only if the `/_index` count does not exceed [the settle windows that held a `change` event]" compares two quantities that cannot be equal on a correct implementation: the crew view's own first paint fetches `/_index` before `/_discover` (§4), and that request sits behind no change event, so a quiet 30 minutes reads ≥1 against 0 settle windows and the section fails however well it was built; the second quantity is also not in the log the clause names, because a change stream is one logged request, not one line per event

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_attach_schedule_for_read` resolves at `reckon/serve.py:1777` (swallows a crew-row failure and returns 200 with `schedule` null and `schedule_error`, as the bullet claims), the shell's 3 s `/crew` poll resolves at `docs/ui/shell.jsx:298`, and `tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py` exists with `BOUND = 50_000` against `reckon/serve.py`'s measured 46,049 estimated tokens.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11's crew case asserts a render and drives the shell's poll and minute timer, but no declared write path hosts a harness that can run it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §11 places every log under the run directory, and its acceptance count is read from the served request log rather than a scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches §11's new symbols; `DERIVED_STATE_KEYS`, `/_schedule/<project>` and `reckon:derived` name the mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold. The root cause matches the cited code: `docs/ui/state-loader.js:747-758` dispatches `reckon-fleet` and then calls `refetchDerived()` on every `fleet` event, and `_attach_schedule_for_read` builds the schedule from live crew rows, so the plan's claim that fleet events are today the only path a run change reaches the derived flow is supported by what it cites. Each bullet's mechanism is capable of its measure, and the caller is named and real: the `/_crew` poll at `docs/ui/shell.jsx:298` returns rows carrying `project`, `plan` and `phase` (`reckon/serve.py:805-826`), so the crew view can indeed see a run-set or phase change and drive the `/_index`-free `/_schedule` fetch.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11's three bullets are one behaviour (route, its two consumers, removal of the fleet-driven refetch) and each now carries its own control.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §11 declares `depends-on the-page-paints-from-an-index#s10` (`plan-section-depends-on`), which matches its prose "Build it after §10, which writes the same files".
